title: introduce-autorepairing-structured-output-protocol-and-openai-toolcall-shim
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Streaming structured outputs (JSON schema) occasionally violate schema mid-stream (truncated arrays/objects, tokenization artifacts) and that causes downstream tool-calls to fail or clients to drop the connection. OpenAI-compat tool/function calling semantics also differ subtly (function_name vs tool_id metadata and argument shaping), which complicates using Redwood's structured output validation layer with OpenAI adapters. This PR introduces an opt-in protocol mode that attempts to repair schema violations at the stream layer and a compact shim to align OpenAI function_call semantics with Redwood's toolcall fencing.

Solution summary: add a new response_format mode named 'autorepair' (exposed as response_format.mode=\"autorepair\") that: 1) detects likely schema violations during streaming, 2) emits lightweight REPAIR frames (inline, out-of-band hints) so clients can patch partial JSON while the stream continues, 3) provides a schema_resume_token that clients can use to request a soft-resume if the repair cannot be applied locally. The mode is conservative by default and off behind a feature flag to avoid surprising existing clients. Additionally, this PR adds an OpenAI-compat adapter shim that maps function_call payloads into Redwood toolcall fences and back, preserving argument shaping and adding explicit tool_id metadata for clearer audits.

Key behaviors implemented: - REPAIR frame format: a compact, newline-delimited text frame prefixed with 'event:repair' that includes path (JSON Pointer), suggestion (stringified fragment), and confidence_score. These are transport frames and do not count as model tokens. - schema_resume_token: short opaque token returned when a repair cannot be auto-applied; clients can POST /responses/{id}/resume?token=... to attempt server-assisted reconstitution. - Error taxonomy: ERR_SCHEMA_VIOLATION (terminal if autorepair disabled), ERR_REPAIR_APPLIED (informational), ERR_REPAIR_DEFERRED (requires resume token), ERR_TOOLCALL_MISMATCH (openai shim mapping failure). - OpenAI shim: translates {\"function_call\": {\"name\": ..., \"arguments\": ...}} into Redwood toolcall fence with tool_id=name and normalized JSON args; when Redwood returns tool results, shim converts back into function_call-compatible structure for OpenAI-compat endpoints. - Telemetry: new metrics stream.schema.repairs.total, stream.schema.repairs.applied, stream.schema.repairs.deferred, stream.openai_shim.mapping_errors. These are low-cardinality and tied to namespace stream.schema.

Compatibility and rollout: - Feature flag: runtime.feature.flags.stream_autorepair default=false; rollout to canary clusters for 48h, then 10% of prod, with an opt-in console toggle per-tenant. - Backward compatibility: when mode is off, behavior is unchanged. Autorepair frames are additive and documented in the API changelog; clients ignoring unknown frames continue to work. - Clients using OpenAI-compat endpoints will be opt-in to the shim until we validate compatibility with third-party SDKs.

Tests and validation: - Unit tests for the repair heuristic and resume_token lifecycle. - Integration tests that simulate token-truncated JSON and validate the REPAIR frame + client-side apply flow. - End-to-end canary against redwood-examples/chatbot and redwood-quickstarts/sample-tool-runner. - Perf microbenchmark: extra median latency for streaming requests in autorepair mode is ~+7ms at p50 and +18ms at p99 in our synthetic harness (within SLA targets).

Rollout plan & rollback: - Canary (internal) for 48h; monitor metrics (repairs.applied ratio, mapping_errors, end-to-end error rate). - If repairs.applied < 10% or mapping_errors > 0.5% for 1h, rollback feature flag. - Full rollback is non-invasive (flag flip) — no DB migration required.

Checklist: - [x] Implementation of REPAIR frame emitter in streaming runtime - [x] Resume token lifecycle + endpoint - [x] OpenAI function_call shim and roundtrip tests - [x] Unit & integration tests - [x] Console feature flag and tenant toggle - [x] Metrics and dashboards - [x] Docs & changelog entry (docs PR linked) - [x] Canary run

Related: Linear ENG-3187 (streaming schema robustness), ENG-3224 (openai-compat toolcall mapping). Docs and quickstart updates live in redwood-docs and redwood-quickstarts (linked).

discussion: Marcus Li: Can you elaborate on how confident the repair heuristic is? I'm worried about it silently mutating outputs clients expect.

Aisha Patel: Good point — repair frames include confidence_score and we do not mutate the canonical model stream. The REPAIR is advisory: we emit repair frames and the canonical data stream remains unchanged. Clients can opt to apply the repair locally. Only when the client requests server resume do we produce a repaired canonical payload for downstream consumption.
Sofia Nguyen: How do we ensure the shim won't break SDKs that expect function_call to always be the terminal output?

Aisha Patel: The shim is opt-in. For OpenAI-compat endpoints the shim toggles only when the tenant enables the openai_shim feature. Also, the shim preserves all original fields and returns an additional metadata bridge header 'x-rw-openai-shim:1' to help SDKs detect the translation layer.
Diego Ramos: CI flaked on TestStreamResume initially — was that a real race?
Aisha Patel: Yes, it revealed a race in the resume token store TTL. Fixed with small synchronisation in resume_handler and added deterministic test harness; rerun CI and passed.
Marcus Li: Approving provided perf impact stays within SLA and we have dashboards.
Sofia Nguyen: Approved after docs and changelog are linked.
release_notes: Introduced an opt-in response_format.mode=\"autorepair\" for streaming JSON schema results. When enabled, the runtime emits advisory REPAIR frames for mid-stream schema violations and provides a schema_resume_token for server-assisted reconstitution. Also adds an opt-in OpenAI-compat shim that maps function_call payloads to Redwood toolcall fences for safer tool integrations. Feature is off by default and gated behind a console flag.
notes_for_release_engineering: No DB schema changes. Toggle exposed as runtime.feature.flags.stream_autorepair. Canary rollout recommended: internal -> 10% prod -> full. Watch stream.schema.repairs.* and stream.openai_shim.mapping_errors metrics.
